title: Added a Pearl Pulse stun weapon to my underwater game
author: jsuffolk
selftext:
Been working on the gameplay feel and added a “Pearl Pulse,” which shows up about halfway through the clip. It stuns enemies, with different effects depending on what you hit.

I’ve been trying to keep the game about avoidance and getting through dangerous areas, not a shooter. I might still add a few weapon-like powerups or utility upgrades later, maybe a gravity gun that can sometimes be used offensively.

I want to give the sub more tricks while still keeping it mostly about avoidance. I'd love to hear feedback on what you all think of the weapons/gameplay.

comments.author: BrotherMoy
comments.body: How'd you get the art style consistent and also animate everything?

replies.author: jsuffolk
replies.body:
I use a few tricks for art style consistency

1. Use reference images heavily for initial art direction, iterate repeatedly with corrective prompts, targeting specific regions of the images with coordinates to fine tune corrections. I edit manually in the end using traditional image editor to clean up any artifacts, tune color/lighting consistency, or customize if I’m struggling to get the AI to produce the look I want  
2. For certain things I use custom SDXL models, especially the terrain. Training for these is somewhat expensive. For the terrain I use multiple weighted Loras where I can tune the strength to create different tuneable biome looks that I can interpolate between. The terrain model is really slick, turning a human authored silhouette and prompt into full sets of material maps with different selectable biomes that can be interpolated at different weights

For animation I usually use an animation model,  often veo lite, then extract frames, finally convert black to transparency while protecting the interior with a mask
